microsoft/microsoft-decision-1.name: Decision-1
microsoft/microsoft-decision-1.description: Microsoft Decision-1 is a text decision model from Microsoft AI for classification, routing, and evaluation. It answers yes/no questions, selects among predefined options, and scores inputs against custom criteria, returning calibrated probabilities and confidence values. With support for multiple questions per request and a 32,768-token context window, it helps developers triage support requests, guide automated workflows, and evaluate AI responses against a rubric.

perplexity/pplx-decider-flash-v1.2.name: Decider Flash V1.2 4B
perplexity/pplx-decider-flash-v1.2.description: Perplexity Decider Flash V1.2 is a 4B multimodal decision model for high-volume classification, routing, labeling, and filtering. It evaluates text, structured JSON, and images against yes/no questions, custom choices, and ordered rubrics, returning typed answers with probabilities. It supports a 256K context window.

perplexity/pplx-decider-v1.2.name: Decider V1.2 27B
perplexity/pplx-decider-v1.2.description: Perplexity Decider V1.2 is a 27B multimodal decision model for classification, routing, and scoring. It evaluates text, structured JSON, and images against yes/no questions, custom choices, and ordered rubrics, returning typed answers with probabilities. It supports multiple questions over shared content and a 256K context window.

baseten/mammoth-1.name: Mammoth-1
baseten/mammoth-1.description: Mammoth-1 is a 27B evaluation model from Baseten's Base Labs, fine-tuned from Qwen3.5-27B for classification, routing, and scoring. It answers multiple-choice, yes/no, and ordered scoring questions with probabilities over predefined options rather than generated text. Shared-prefix caching reuses context across questions, while per-option probabilities support confidence thresholds and escalation decisions.

baseten/elephant-1.name: Elephant-1
baseten/elephant-1.description: Elephant-1 is a 9B evaluation model from Baseten's Base Labs for classification, routing, and scoring. It evaluates structured context against choice, yes/no, and ordered scoring questions and returns answer probabilities and confidence in a single forward pass, without generating free-form text. Applications can use these probabilities to select answers or set confidence thresholds.

baseten/joey-1.name: Joey-1
baseten/joey-1.description: Joey-1 is a 2B decision model from Baseten's Base Labs for classification, routing, and scoring. It evaluates text context against choice, yes/no, and ordered scoring questions, returning answer probabilities and confidence in a single forward pass without generating free-form text.

openai/gpt-6-luna-decisions.name: GPT-6 Luna Decisions
openai/gpt-6-luna-decisions.description: GPT-6 Luna Decisions evaluates classification and scoring questions against shared text and image input using OpenAI's Decisions API. It supports predicate, choice, and score questions with probabilities and confidence values.

liquid/d1-ultra.name: Liquid d1 Ultra
liquid/d1-ultra.description: Liquid d1-ultra is a multimodal decision model for classification, routing, and scoring across text and images, with a 32,768-token context window. It returns calibrated probabilities for yes/no, multiple-choice, and scale-based questions in a single forward pass without generating output tokens. It is designed for demanding real-world tasks such as visual defect inspection and evaluating damage claims against customer photos.

liquid/d1.name: Liquid d1
liquid/d1.description: System One decision model for typed classification, routing, and scoring over shared state

nace-ai/drex-max-finance.name: Drex Max Finance
nace-ai/drex-max-finance.description: Drex Max Finance is Nace AI's multimodal evaluation model for financial workflows. It answers boolean, choice, and score questions over text and images with calibrated probabilities. Its 262,144-token limit covers the whole request, including shared state, images, questions, formatting, and decision markers.

nace-ai/drex-max-v1.1.name: Drex Max v1.1
nace-ai/drex-max-v1.1.description: Drex Max v1.1 is Nace AI's multimodal evaluation model for boolean, choice, and score questions over text and images. It returns structured answers and probability distributions. Its 262,144-token limit applies to the whole packed request, including shared state, images, all questions, formatting, and decision markers.

nace-ai/drex-v2.0.name: Drex 2.0
nace-ai/drex-v2.0.description: 35B mixture-of-experts System One decision model with 3B active parameters, returning typed, calibrated probabilities over text or structured state without generating text

parallel/parallel-decisions-fast.name: Decisions Fast
parallel/parallel-decisions-fast.description: Decisions Fast is Parallel AI’s evaluation model for fast classification and scoring grounded in live web evidence. It answers yes/no, multiple-choice, and ordered scoring questions with probabilities and citations. Each request supports up to 100 related questions sharing the same context and retrieved evidence, with flat per-request pricing.

typesafe-ai/jev-1.14.0.name: Jev 1.14.0
typesafe-ai/jev-1.14.0.description: Jev 1.14.0 is TypeSafe AI’s System One evaluation model for fast, structured decisions in software. It evaluates shared state against typed questions and returns choices, scores, and boolean probabilities, supporting classification, routing, rubric-based assessment, and automated verification. Multiple questions can be evaluated in parallel within a single request.

typesafe-ai/jev-1.13.0.name: Jev 1.13.0
typesafe-ai/jev-1.13.0.description: Jev 1.13.0 is TypeSafe AI’s System One evaluation model for fast, structured decisions in software. It evaluates shared state against typed questions and returns choices, scores, and boolean probabilities, supporting classification, routing, rubric-based assessment, and automated verification. Multiple questions can be evaluated in parallel within a single request.

Its deterministic, encoder-only approach produces consistent classification results without sampling variability.
